title: Lord of the Mysteries | خداوندانِ اسرار | SufiPulse USA
description:
LORD OF THE MYSTERIES
خداوندانِ اسرار

An immersive Persian-inspired Sufi composition by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori, presented by SufiPulse USA.

Built around the invocation:

“Khuda, raazdaraan-e-raazdaaran…”

God, Keeper of the keepers of secrets.

Lord of the Mysteries enters the contemplative atmosphere of Persian mysticism, zikr, sama‘, and the inward journey of seekers drawn toward Divine remembrance.

Its language moves through Noor within Noor, hidden gatherings, inward longing, dissolution of ego, and the orbit of lovers around the Muhammadan Light ﷺ.

At its spiritual center stands:

“Aaftaab-e-Noor”
The Sun of Divine Light ﷺ

Here, Noor-e-Muhammadi ﷺ is approached symbolically through the devotional language of light.

“Raaz-e-nihaani-e dar seena-am furood aawar…
Ke dil bar aahang-e-aan, baarahaa be raqs aayad…”

“Place within my chest a hidden mystery,
whose rhythm makes this heart dance again and again.”

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WHY THIS WORK

SufiPulse USA creates sacred media for remembrance, reflection, and awakening.

Lord of the Mysteries asks what happens when longing moves beyond explanation and enters rhythm, repetition, silence, and surrender.

The work unfolds in two movements:

Part I — longing, hidden mysteries, and Divine Light.

Part II — a sama‘-inspired passage into deeper remembrance.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

This composition draws inspiration from classical Persian irfaan and the spiritual atmosphere associated with Jalal al-Din Rumi, Shams-e-Tabriz, zikr, and sama‘.

It does not reproduce their writings or claim direct lineage from them.

Persian imagery, cinematic sound, repetition, and symbolism are used to create an original contemporary Sufi work.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WRITER’S NOTE

References to Noor-e-Muhammadi ﷺ and “Aaftaab-e-Noor” are devotional and mystical symbolism.

They are not presented as scientific propositions or as a single theological interpretation binding all Muslim traditions.

Here, light becomes a language for guidance, love, awakening, and remembrance.

The seeker approaches through adab.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: Laut A | Sufi Science Center USA Inaugural Anthem | SufiPulse USA
description:
LAUT A
Website Inaugural Promo | Sufi Science Center USA | SufiPulse USA

An original Sufi call written by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori and presented by SufiPulse USA for the inauguration of Sufi Science Center USA.

“Laut A” — Return.

Not backward in time, but inward toward inheritance, remembrance, responsibility, and purpose.

The song calls the next generation of Kashmiris and global seekers to carry Kashmir’s Sufi inheritance forward through science, profession, creativity, leadership, service, and modern inquiry.

The saints of Kashmir still whisper through rivers, shrines, mountains, memory, poetry, and conscience.

The question is not whether the past can be recreated, but whether its light can be carried forward.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WHY THIS WORK

Sufi Science Center USA was conceived as a next-generation space where inherited Sufi wisdom can meet contemporary life without becoming nostalgia or spectacle.

Laut A gives that vision a voice.

“Rise in your profession as prayer.
Lead in your duty as dhikr.
Carry your inheritance as Noor.”

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

Return does not mean abandoning science, technology, education, or professional life.

It means rejecting the false choice between spiritual inheritance and modern competence.

Its language is contemporary because the next generation must be reached in its own style, profession, and tone.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WRITER’S NOTE

“Sufi Science” does not mean that mystical or devotional claims automatically become scientific facts.

It describes a space where spiritual traditions, ethics, consciousness, culture, human experience, and modern knowledge may meet with intellectual honesty.

Faith and science are not collapsed into one another. Each retains its methods, limits, and integrity.

Laut A is a call to integration — not confusion.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: Aahista Aahista | Teach Your Soul How to Flow | SufiPulse USA
description:
AAHISTA AAHISTA
Teach Your Soul How to Flow

A contemplative Kashmiri Sufi journey presented by SufiPulse USA, inspired by the mystical traditions of Kashmir and Kishtwar.

At its poetic heart stands Janbaz Kishtwari (Ghulam Nabi Doolwal), whose remembered kalam carries the seeker through longing, surrender, silence, and the slow opening of the soul.

Its musical memory honors Ustad Abdul Samad Sofi — Samad Saib — whose Chalant-style voice and spiritual intensity helped carry this kalam through generations of Kashmiri Sufi remembrance.

SufiPulse adopts only the line:

“Aahista, Aahista, Madanwar Yokun, Kadam Akh Traav”

as a humble bridge between inherited Kashmiri Sufi expression and a contemporary sacred-media form.

The path does not open by force.
The soul does not ripen by command.
The Beloved is approached… aahista.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WHY THIS WORK

Aahista Aahista asks the seeker to slow the inner noise before asking where the Beloved is.

Where is the hidden secret?
Why does the soul remain restless?
Why does love burn before it heals?
Who is speaking from within?
Why must the seeker walk slowly?

The path was never far — only hidden beneath the self. The Beloved was never silent — only covered by inner noise.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

This release is not a replacement for the inherited Kashmiri kalam or its earlier musical life. It is respectful continuation.

The remembered line “Madanwar Yokun, Kadam Akh Traav” becomes the threshold: one step, gently placed.

From there, the contemporary work develops its own meditation on silence, surrender, longing, remembrance, and inward awakening.

“Rooh ko behna seekh zara.”

Teach your soul how to flow.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WRITER’S NOTE

This work distinguishes inspiration from authorship.

Janbaz Kishtwari is honored as the poetic source of the inherited line that inspired this release.

Ustad Abdul Samad Sofi is honored for the musical memory through which the kalam continued to live in Kashmiri consciousness.

SufiPulse USA adopts only the identified line and develops an original contemporary meditation around it.

The intention is respectful renewal — not substitution or erasure of lineage.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: Rehmat Se Likha Khwaab Na Meri Quwwat | SufiPulse USA
description:
REHMAT SE LIKHA KHWAAB NA MERI QUWWAT
A Dream Written by Mercy — Not by My Strength

An original Sufi reflection by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori, presented by SufiPulse USA.

Rehmat Se Likha Khwaab Na Meri Quwwat emerges from a dream connected with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

The work reflects upon the dream’s impression: presence, countenance, bearing, beauty, and the emotional memory that remained after waking.

Its central confession is contained in the title:

“Rehmat se likha khwaab, na meri quwwat.”

A dream written by mercy — not by my strength.

The kalam does not present the experience as spiritual accomplishment. Whatever was recognized was received, not earned. Its purpose is remembrance, love, reverence, humility, and gratitude.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WHY THIS WORK

SufiPulse USA creates sacred media for remembrance, reflection, and awakening.

Some spiritual experiences are too intimate for ordinary narration yet too meaningful for silence. This kalam preserves such an experience without trying to prove it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

The physical and noble qualities associated with Prophet Muhammad ﷺ belong to the revered tradition of Shamā’il-e-Muhammadiyya — the inherited body of transmitted descriptions.

This kalam draws upon that devotional vocabulary while remaining an artistic work.

It does not manufacture a visual portrait or turn a private dream into religious evidence.

Reverence before spectacle.
Transmission before invention.
Humility before claim.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WRITER’S NOTE

What is expressed here is transmission, not testimony.

The lyrics arise from mercy — a dream, not sight.

No claim is made of authoritative vision, proximity, spiritual rank, or worth.

The dream is remembered as a personal devotional experience, approached through inherited Shamā’il language and the dreamer’s emotional recognition.

A private spiritual experience may inspire poetry and remembrance without becoming proof for anyone else.

Recognition itself is mercy.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: PANI GAWAH HAI | KASHMIR WATER BEARS WITNESS | SufiPulse USA
description:
PANI GAWAH HAI
KASHMIR WATER BEARS WITNESS

An original contemporary Sufi environmental advocacy kalam by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori, presented by SufiPulse USA.

Today, rivers are dammed, lakes encroached upon, wetlands buried beneath concrete, springs fall silent, forests vanish and glaciers retreat. Yet while humanity debates development and progress, the waters continue to flow — bearing witness to every decision we make.

PANI GAWAH HAI transforms water from a resource into a moral and spiritual witness.

The kalam journeys through Kashmir’s ecological soul — Dal Lake, Nigeen, Wular, the Jhelum, Khushal Sar, Bari Nambal, Anchar, Hokersar, Shallabugh, Haigam, Himalayan springs and glaciers.

But this is not only Kashmir’s story. It is the story of every polluted river, disappearing wetland and generation inheriting a quieter Earth.

From a Sufi perspective, creation carries Ayat — signs inviting remembrance, humility and responsibility.

If water bears witness, what will it remember about us?

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WHY THIS WORK

SufiPulse USA creates sacred media for remembrance, reflection and awakening.

PANI GAWAH HAI brings that purpose into spirituality and ecology. Kashmir’s waters are not scenery alone; they have shaped memory, livelihood, poetry and civilization.

This work asks whether stewardship can again be understood as moral responsibility.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

This is neither a protest song nor a political slogan.

The production could have foregrounded sewage, pollution, encroachment and ecological humiliation. We chose restraint.

Kashmir’s waters have witnessed enough. They do not need to be publicly shamed to prove what they already know.

Sometimes the strongest testimony is not what we expose, but what we protect with dignity.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WRITER’S NOTE

Water remembers.
Mountains remember.
Forests remember.
The Earth remembers.

“Water Bears Witness” is a spiritual and poetic metaphor for accountability and consequence — not a scientific claim that water literally records human actions.

Will future generations inherit rivers of life — or rivers of regret?

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: Husain Andar – Yazeed Andar | Kise Doon Main Aasra | SufiPulse USA
description:
HUSAIN ANDAR – YAZEED ANDAR
Kise Doon Main Aasra

An original mystical Sufi kalam by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori, presented by SufiPulse USA.

What if Karbala did not end in 680 CE? What if its most enduring battlefield is the human heart?

This is not a historical retelling of Karbala. It is a spiritual meditation on the struggle within every human being.

Here, Yazeed symbolizes the crowned ego — the “I” that seeks power over truth. Husain symbolizes the awakened conscience — the light within that refuses to bow before falsehood.

Every heart becomes a battlefield. Every relationship becomes a mirror.

If pride makes a mother weep, arrogance bends a father, neglect turns siblings into strangers, a spouse loses peace, trust disappears from friendship, or authority strips another person of dignity — who truly rules within us?

The battlefield is within.
The throne is within.
The choice is within.

“Main” se “Tu” tak — bas ye safar.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WHY THIS WORK

This work brings Karbala inward. It asks us to stop treating moral courage as something belonging only to history and to examine the throne of the present heart.

Every morning a Yazeed can rise.
Every morning a Husain can awaken.

Who is the king of your heart today?

When the ego falls, the soul rises.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

Yazeed Andar — the crowned ego that demands obedience and places power above truth.

Husain Andar — the awakened conscience that refuses surrender to falsehood.

Karbala Andar — the inner battlefield where ego and conscience meet.

“Karbala is not confined to dust. Where the ego demands a crown and conscience asks for surrender, there Karbala awakens again.”

This is a mystical interpretation, not a replacement for the historical reality of Karbala.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WRITER’S NOTE

The editorial team paused over one question: Imam Husain (RA) or Imam Husain (AS)?

Although rooted in the Sunni tradition, we chose Imam Husain (AS) here not as a sectarian statement, but as an expression of reverence.

If this kalam asks us to overcome ego, then knowledge itself must not become an ego.

Sometimes the first Karbala is in the editor’s own heart.

“Main mita to Noor mila.
Yahi Husain... Yahi Karbala.”

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: Wanun Traav Hunar Haav | Kashmiri Sufi Poetry | SufiPulse USA
description:
KEMIS TAANI CHHU AAV AAV
A Kashmiri-English Sufi Kalam

An original contemporary Sufi kalam by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori, presented by SufiPulse USA.

Kemis Taani Chhu Aav Aav is built around a call rather than an explanation.

“Kemis taani chhu aav aav.”

For whom has the presence arrived?
For whom does the call come?

The composition does not answer for the listener. It turns the listener inward.

Its English passages open the meaning, while two adopted Kashmiri verses associated with Mahjoor preserve the sound, rhythm, and spiritual weight of the Kashmiri source tradition.

The Kashmiri lines are not ornamental. They are the spiritual anchor of the work.

The English verses open the meaning.
The Kashmiri verses carry the presence.

Words begin to fall away.
Silence begins to speak.
The seeker begins to listen.

The call you hear is not outside.
It is rising from within.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WHY THIS WORK

SufiPulse USA creates sacred media for remembrance, reflection, and awakening.

This work was shaped for listeners who may not speak Kashmiri but still seek its spiritual and emotional world.

Rather than translate everything into English, Kashmiri and English coexist.

One language explains.
The other remembers.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

Two verses from Mahjoor’s kalam are retained because their cadence and cultural memory carry something translation alone cannot reproduce.

They are not decoration. They form the point of return for the contemporary English composition.

Adaptation should acknowledge lineage rather than erase it.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

◆ WRITER’S NOTE

“Bulbul chhu baraan” is acknowledged as adopted material from Mahjoor’s poetic tradition.

The contemporary English composition, framing, and interpretive journey are by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori.

The purpose is not to claim inherited poetry, but to carry its living sound into a new linguistic setting.

The call remains Kashmiri.
The listening becomes universal.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

title: Main Hoon Ya Khwaab Hoon
description: Main Hoon Ya Khwaab Hoon explores the uncertain boundary between identity, consciousness, perception and the world we call reality. Is the self the dreamer, or merely another image appearing within the dream? The work approaches that question through contemporary Sufi expression, placing mystical inquiry within a modern musical language.

title: PEHCHAAN KHUD KO
description:
PEHCHAAN KHUD KO
Recognize Yourself

An original Sufi reflection by Dr. Zarf-e-Noori, presented by SufiPulse USA.

Pehchaan Khud Ko is an inward call to the seeker who has learned to read the world but not yet the self.

“Kise dhoond raha hai shehron ki gard mein?
Jise sadiyon se pukaar raha hai,
wo teri hi saans mein hai.”

Its central question:

MAIN KAUN HOON?

The kalam moves from outward search toward inward recognition, asking what remains beneath name, image, fear, status, memory, and borrowed identity.

“Tu aainon mein chehra padhta raha,
rooh ki tehreer na padh saka.”

The work does not ask the listener to invent a new self. It asks us to remember, recognize, and move.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
◆ WHY THIS WORK

SufiPulse USA creates sacred media for remembrance, reflection, and awakening.

We spend years measuring the world and collecting answers while one question remains unfinished:

“Tu ne har sawaal ka jawaab likha,
bas main kaun hoon adhoora chhoda.”

Pehchaan Khud Ko turns that question inward.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
◆ EDITORIAL NOTE

This kalam is a mystical reflection on self-recognition.

Its language of rooh, noor, fana, identity, loss, and remembrance belongs to the contemplative vocabulary of the Sufi path. It is not a theological definition of the self or a claim of spiritual rank.

Recognition before proclamation.
Remembrance before reinvention.
Humility before identity.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
◆ WRITER’S NOTE

We recognize faces, professions, beliefs, wounds, and ambitions — and eventually mistake them for the whole self.

This kalam asks what remains when those descriptions become silent.

“Jab parde girenge, chehre nahi bachenge.
Jab naam mitenge, rutbe nahi bachenge.
Ek hi sawaal bachega...
kya tu ne khud ko pehchaana?”

Not every fall is punishment. Not every loss is annihilation.

“Kabhi kabhi Rabb tujhe tujhse milaane ko
tujhse sab chheen leta hai.”

The final instruction is not withdrawal.

Pehchaan khud ko.
Aur chal pad.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
